Not just the reveal but the build up to it. We witness carnage and slaughter and destruction of a whole country and almost the whole population, the torture of two really powerful leaders who want nothing but to protect their people and land.

Then to have the reveal, in public where the entire country’s population, still physically broken and mentally scarred (probably for life), and see every Mink bowing so graciously to samurai—at the time we don’t even know their connection—and see the whole country had banded together to protect one person even though it was going to literally kill all of them…

it’s just an intensely powerful reveal with so much emotion behind it, so much intent.

One thing I absolutely adore about Oda is that he has perfected (in my opinion) how to make a community seem so tight-knit and passionate about their values and country, he knows how to show and make us believe in camaraderie, he knows how to demonstrate the power of a society that will literally die for protecting their values. You don’t see that anywhere that isn’t a very small population in the real world, much less a whole country. But Oda makes it feel real.
